biggestGap: Every outline event this piece owns is authored ON THE POLAR AXIS — calyx, stem, crown, navel, spur — so a fruit is nameable only in the poses that happen to show a pole, and the round's single largest mesh gain proves it: the apple calyx (len 0.110 -> 0.225) moved `limb pose=ship` hull_concave_frac_pct 41.80 -> 50.78 and protr_height_pct 8.15 -> 13.10, and in the SHIPPED pixels of 11-combo+550ms it delivered hull_concave_frac_pct 24.22 -> 25.78 landscape and 62.50 -> 59.38 portrait (DOWN), because in neither pose is the calyx pole toward camera; the equatorial profile between the poles is still an exact solid of revolution and reads as a lathe in a still.
evidence:
PROBE DISCIPLINE FIRST. I MODIFIED NOTHING. I ADDED ONE PROBE, `outline`, and bumped PROBE_VERSION 11 -> 12 (the fruit-mat critic had already taken 10 -> 11 concurrently this round; I re-verified the canary at BOTH). Canary under v12: `clip shots/r5/05-cut+500ms.png` -> mask_px 9490 / pct_R_ge_255 5.227. Verified rather than asserted: the full suite was captured on shots/r5, r8, r9, r8-iphone and r9-iphone under v11, the edit made, the suite re-run and diffed key-by-key on all five — every pre-existing row byte-identical, only `outline:01-whole-watermelon.png` appears. r8 geometry re-derived, not quoted, from tools/geometry-r8-critic-snapshot.js (git 82017c4, same convention as the existing r5/r6/r7 snapshots) via `species src=` / `limb src=`.

1. THE INSTRUMENT AUDIT. I AGREE WITH THE BUILDER, AND THE DECISIVE NUMBER IS STRONGER THAN THE ONE IT QUOTED. `species pose=so3 n=32 rays=128 res=256` on the r8 geometry — the geometry my own r8 verdict said silhouetted as five unnameable ovals — returns identity_accuracy 0.9948, identity_recall 1.000 for watermelon/orange/kiwi/apple/strawberry and 0.969 for the pineapple. r9 returns 0.9792 (recall kiwi 0.938, pineapple 0.938). Total dynamic range across the entire round: 191/192 -> 188/192 poses. A metric that scores 99.5% on geometry a human cannot name is not measuring nameability. But the killer is finer than saturation: in r8 the ORANGE was provably featureless — `limb pose=so3 n=32` gives hull_concave_frac_pct EXACTLY 0.00, boundary_cv_median 0.008, elongation_median 1.011, i.e. a convex sphere in every one of 32 poses — and its identity_recall was 1.000. `identity` awards a perfect score to a mathematical sphere. THE DEEPER CLAIM IS THEREFORE CONFIRMED: identity is a 6-way CLOSED-SET 1-NN whose only referent is the other five bodies, all of which we authored, so six smooth ellipsoids at six aspect ratios would also score 1.000. Self-consistency cannot measure resemblance to a real apple. `identity` remains a good CONTROL (it is not gameable by deletion, unlike `separation`, and it caught the builder's kiwi/melon spur collision) and a useless TARGET.

2. THE EXTERNAL REFERENT: I TRIED TO BUILD IT, IT DOES NOT WORK BY AUTO-SEGMENTATION, AND THE NEGATIVE RESULT IS MEASURED AND WRITTEN INTO probes.py SO THE NEXT AGENT DOES NOT REPEAT IT. Real apple in reference/plate-01.png, box (848,108)-(1132,358), subject floor 20 + largest_component: a clean nameable mask — stem spur, shoulder notch, leaf — but juice filaments bridge it to the splash at three box edges, so the traced signature is the splash's. Break the bridges morphologically and the SAME operation eats the feature: a k=3 opening drops the mask bbox height 243 -> 225 px, and that 18 px IS the stem, because a real juice filament and a real apple stalk are both ~3 px wide in this plate. Real strawberry, box (1285,428)-(1515,620): its own body sits BELOW the subject floor while the juice around it sits above — at floor 20 the mask is the splash with a fruit-shaped HOLE in it (a luma floor is not a colour key, but on a dark fruit in a black void it behaves like one). CONCLUSION: the referent must be a small set of HAND-TRACED outline polygons frozen into probes.py as literals, not an auto-segmentation of a splash composite. I did not ship a traced set because I was not willing to author, and then score against, my own ground truth inside one round with nobody to check it. It is the highest-value thing left in this instrument.

3. WHAT I ADDED INSTEAD, AND THE SEAM IT IMMEDIATELY CAUGHT. `limb` measures the MESH; `silhouette` measures the FRAME; they share no statistic, so a mesh gain and a frame loss could not be put in the same sentence. `outline` (v12) calls the frozen `_limb_stats` — byte for byte, same thr=0.02, same k<=3 Fourier baseline, same `_hull_radii` — on a radial signature traced from delivered pixels, mask geometric (`subject_mask` + `largest_component`, optional explicit `win=x0:y0:x1:y1` as `foam`/`collar` take theirs), mask_px reported. FROZEN WINDOWS, IDENTICAL BOTH ROUNDS, on 11-combo+550ms:
  apple  win=378:175:490:275  hull_frac 24.22 -> 25.78, hull_depth 7.92 -> 5.88 (DOWN 26%), protr_height 2.65 -> 3.25
  straw  win=270:275:350:352  hull_frac 58.59 -> 68.75, hull_depth 20.13 -> 37.03, protr_height 16.53 -> 25.02, protr_height_max 19.01 -> 35.92
  kiwi   win=510:255:632:360  hull_frac 12.50 -> 19.53, hull_depth 10.40 -> 13.78

  apple PORTRAIT win=145:230:215:295  hull_frac 62.50 -> 59.38 (DOWN), hull_depth 17.88 -> 22.21
Against `limb pose=ship n=32` on the same two meshes: apple hull_frac 41.80 -> 50.78 (+8.98 pp mesh) vs +1.56 pp landscape pixels and -3.12 pp portrait pixels; apple hull_depth 45.59 -> 45.05 mesh vs 7.92 -> 5.88 in pixels. The apple's +112 triangles bought nothing a player sees, in EITHER orientation.

4. AND I CHECKED THE OBVIOUS ALTERNATIVE EXPLANATION AND IT IS NOT A THRESHOLD BUG. Sweeping the subject floor on the identical apple crop: floor 8 -> r8 max_protrusion 12.62 / r9 12.41; floor 4 -> 15.11 / 12.19; floor 2 -> 25.07 / 24.71; floor 1 -> 24.31 / 24.31. r9 equals or trails r8 at EVERY floor. The calyx is not dim, it is absent from those pixels. That is pose, not shading — so this is NOT the r8-class 'shader clamped the mask away' bug, and I say so plainly.

5. THE CONTROL THAT PROVES THE PIPELINE IS NOT EATING FEATURES GENERALLY, so item 3 is specific and not a smear. Watermelon, uncut, 01-whole-watermelon, the new suite row: mesh `limb pose=ship` hull_concave_depth_pct 7.64 -> 10.22 (+2.58); frame landscape 7.70 -> 9.70 (+2.00); frame PORTRAIT 10.00 -> 12.58 (+2.58). The melon's mesh gain transfers to pixels at 0.78-1.00x. The apple's transfers at 0.17x landscape and negative in portrait. Same renderer, same round.

6. THE REAL WIN, STATED FIRST AMONG THE PICTURE FINDINGS BECAUSE IT IS THE BIGGEST THIS PIECE HAS HAD. The strawberry calyx is back OUTSIDE the waist and it reads at shipping pixel size. On the r8 verdict's own frozen crop (280,275)-(345,340) of 09-combo+50ms, `silhouette`: max_protrusion_pct 21.50 -> 29.46, boundary_cv 0.1019 -> 0.1172 — about half the r7->r8 loss recovered (r7 was 40.29) while keeping the sepals the CORRECT colour, which r7 did not. On 11-combo, max_protrusion 19.92 -> 32.65. Rendered flat white at luma>8 at 4x, the r9 strawberry has three or four unmistakable spikes off the shoulder where r8 had one 1-2 px nick. IT IS THE FIRST FRUIT IN THIS PROJECT I CAN NAME FROM ITS OUTLINE ALONE. And two species that were mathematically convex are no longer: orange hull_concave_frac_pct 0.00 -> 16.41 and kiwi 0.00 -> 12.50 over 32 uniform SO(3) poses.

7. THE DECISIVE QUESTION, ANSWERED HONESTLY, BOTH ORIENTATIONS. shots/r9/11-combo+550ms thresholded at the probe's own luma>8 floor and rendered flat white, four resolvable fruit: strawberry YES (spikes, unmistakable); kiwi PARTLY — it gained a spur, but as a mask it is a ragged tuft of disconnected islands that reads as breakage or a rendering artefact rather than a stalk scar, and a real kiwifruit has no tuft at all; apple NO — a smooth blob, visually indistinguishable from its r8 self; pineapple cap NO — a featureless oval, untouched this round. Portrait is where the apple is BEST — shots/r9-iphone/11-combo+550ms shows a stem well and an asymmetric heart profile — which is the point of the biggest gap: it is pose luck, not authored robustness. Two of four nameable is a real move from r8's one of six, and it is not enough.

8. I VERIFIED THE BUILDER'S REFUSAL AND IT IS CORRECT, INCLUDING ITS REASON. It declined my r8 apple fix (tilt the stalk off-axis) on the ground that a crown blade is a radial bump tapering to a point while the profile stem is a constant-width tapered cylinder, and quoted the measured cost: hull_concave_frac_pct 36.72 -> 26.56, hull_concave_depth_pct 35.28 -> 17.14, identity_recall 1.000 -> 0.938, +324 triangles, for a hair instead of a stalk. My r8 `fix` also mis-cited protr_height_pct as 'the stalk'; it is a median over all protrusion runs and the builder is right that it is not. I withdraw that half of my r8 instruction. It took the calyx half, which was the good half, and delivered it in the mesh — item 3 is that it did not reach the frame, which is a different and newly measurable failure.

9. PORTRAIT PERF, AND IT IS NOT MY PIECE — EXACT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. r9-iphone breaches both bars: peakDrawCalls 187 against 120, peakTriangles 266879 against 250k (r8-iphone was 151 / 205747). Landscape r9 went the OTHER way: 113 -> 111 draws, 202659 -> 199753 triangles, and the same mesh ships in both orientations. Triangles per draw call moved 1362 -> 1427 (+4.8%), which is consistent with geometry's declared +2.6% mesh growth; the object COUNT moved 151 -> 187 (+23.8%) and `geometries` 58 -> 85. The portrait breach is an object-count problem in the director/juice/stage path, and geometry contributes roughly a sixth of it. I decline to charge it to this piece, and I decline to let the piece off the +2.6% either.

10. WHAT FAILS IN A STILL THAT WOULD NOT FAIL IN MOTION — the band question. In motion the strawberry's spikes and the melon's spur flicker in and out as the fruit tumble and the eye integrates 'spiky red thing' across frames; the pineapple crown's extent reads regardless. Held still, the eye lands on the outline before the texture and half the fruit are ovals a compass could have drawn — and the specific still-only tell is that the profile between the two poles is EXACTLY mirror-symmetric about its projected axis, because every body is still a solid of revolution plus a linear shear. The builder is right that a shear cannot fix this (an affine image of an axisymmetric silhouette is still an axisymmetric silhouette from another direction) and right to have rejected `bend`. That symmetry, and the pose-lottery it forces on every polar appendage, is the whole remaining distance to 80.

BLIND. shots/r9/11-combo+550ms against reference/plate-01.png is still an instant call and I would not need a second look. On my axis alone the tell has moved once more: it is no longer 'all six are ovals', it is 'the one with spikes is a strawberry and I cannot tell you what the other three are'.
fix: src/fruit/geometry.js — PUT A FEATURE ON THE EQUATOR. The file's own 5A theorem names three mechanisms that can reach a silhouette (axis ratios, plane cuts, appendages) and this piece now uses two of them, both of which live at or near the polar axis; the result is item 3, a large mesh gain that no shipped pose displays. Add the third as a per-species ANGULAR modulation of the profile radius, r(theta, y) = r(y) * (1 + a_k * cos(k*theta + phase(y))), applied in the existing lathe loop for ZERO extra triangles and with star-shapedness preserved by construction (r is still single-valued in theta, so cutter.js's precondition and `star_multivalued_total` 0 are safe). Concretely: apple k=5, a=0.05-0.07 with phase drifting ~0.15 rad from calyx to stem — real apples are genuinely five-lobed in cross-section and it is the one apple cue that survives every pose; kiwi k=2, a=0.06 (a real kiwifruit's section is an ellipse, not a circle); strawberry k=3, a=0.04 on the shoulder band only. Pre-empting the objection: the r5 relief corollary (T^2/8 caps a bump at 0.14% of radius) is about ~3 degrees of arc and does NOT bind a 72-degree lobe, so do not cite it here. THEN CHANGE THE GATE. Stop reporting `limb` alone as evidence that a silhouette improved: it measures the mesh and this round proved that can be +8.98 pp while the shipped pixels are -3.12 pp. Gate on the v12 `outline` probe at the frozen windows quoted above — `outline shots/<dir>/11-combo+550ms.png win=378:175:490:275` for the apple and win=510:255:632:360 for the kiwi — and require hull_concave_depth_pct >= 15 in BOTH orientations for apple and kiwi, a bar the r9 strawberry already clears at 37.03 and the r9 apple fails at 5.88 landscape. Report `limb` and `outline` side by side every round; where they disagree, `outline` wins, because it is the one a player sees.
